author: Ash

copy.intro: You know how a Kohl's run goes. A national brand you trust on one rack, and a cheaper store label like Sonoma Goods for Life or Croft & Barrow on the next. If you want that mix somewhere else, these stores are where to go. Department stores come first, since they're the closest match. After them come the discount stores and off-price chains people shop for the same value, and one family-clothing chain for jeans and basics.

bodies.macys:
Macy's is the closest swap for a full Kohl's trip, with women's, men's and kids' clothing next to beauty and home in one store. Like Kohl's, it sells national names beside its own private labels, so you can trade up or down without leaving the building.

The part worth knowing is Macy's Backstage. It's Macy's own off-price format, run as shops inside Macy's stores and in a few stores of their own, and there are more than 300 of them. So if half the fun of Kohl's is the bargain hunt, look for a Macy's with a Backstage inside and you get both in one stop.

If you'd rather have the off-price hunt without the department store around it, TJ Maxx is the purer version.
bodies.jcpenney:
JCPenney has much the same mix as Kohl's, selling clothing, home, jewelry and beauty under its own labels and national ones. Its stores run across the US and Puerto Rico, so it's an easy walk-in swap if your nearest Kohl's isn't so near.

Start with Liz Claiborne if you buy workwear. JCPenney carries it from petite to plus sizes, with power blazers and pleated trousers among the pieces, in stores and online at JCPenney.com.

That petite-to-plus spread is the reason to look here for office clothes. But if what you mostly buy is jeans and weekend basics, Old Navy's own label goes from size 00 to 30 and shows its prices online.
bodies.dillards:
Dillard's is the pick if you want Kohl's breadth with designer denim on the wall. Women's jeans run from $36 for Celebrity Pink and YMI skinny styles to $350 for Johnny Was embroidered flares, and the brands in between include NYDJ, Levi's and Good American.

Sizes go from 00 to 16 and 1X to 3X, with petite and plus fits, so you can filter by fit before you pick a brand. Some of its stores are clearance centers, so check which kind is near you before you drive.

The catch is reach and shipping. Its stores cover 30 states, against Kohl's 49, and free shipping only starts at $150. If you're buying online, Nordstrom ships free with no minimum.
bodies.nordstrom:
Nordstrom is where to go when you want to trade up from Kohl's without losing the range. Women's jeans start at $20 for the Roaman's Comfort Stretch Wide Leg Jean and climb past $800 for designer denim like Burberry, so one store covers both ends.

Two policies make it easy to try. Shipping is free anywhere in the US with no minimum, and there's no time limit on returns. Jeans sizes run from 00 to 28W, with petite and tall lengths, which goes further up than Dillard's 3X.

If you like the brands but not the prices, the off-price chains below sell name brands for less, and TJ Maxx keeps a designer section for exactly that.
bodies.target:
Target is the everyday swap for Kohl's, with its own labels and national brands side by side in stores in all 50 states. For jeans, start with Universal Thread's Women's High-Rise Vintage Straight Jeans ($38), then compare Levi's High-Rise Cinch Baggy Jeans ($74.99) on the same page.

That's the same pairing Kohl's makes with Sonoma next to the names you know. Target's other owned labels include A New Day and Wild Fable, and the national side runs to Lee and Lucky Brand.

Returns are the quiet perk. Most items get 90 days, and Target's own brands get a full year with a receipt, so buying two sizes and returning one is low-risk.
bodies.tj-maxx:
TJ Maxx is the pick if the brand-name bargain is the reason you shop Kohl's. It's an off-price store, so it sells name brands for women, men and kids, plus beauty and home, for less than full-price stores charge.

Look for The Runway, its high-end designer department in select stores. That's what separates it from Marshalls, its sister chain, which puts its space into shoes and menswear instead. TJ Maxx also sells online, which Ross and Burlington don't.

If shoes are the main errand, Marshalls has the bigger shoe department of the two. And if you know exactly what you want, Target or Old Navy lists it online with a set price.
bodies.ross-dress-for-less:
Ross Dress for Less is the off-price chain for shoppers who'd rather drive than click. It sells name-brand and designer clothing for the whole family, plus shoes and home goods, below what department stores charge.

There's no online shop at all, so this is a store you walk into. What's on the racks varies by store, which makes it a place to browse rather than to hunt one item. With stores in 44 states, it's far easier to find than Dillard's.

If coats are on your list, Burlington is the off-price chain built around them. And if you want to check stock from your couch first, TJ Maxx has a website.
bodies.walmart:
Walmart is the budget end of this list, built on everyday low prices rather than sales events. It sells clothing for adults and kids, plus shoes, jewelry and accessories, in stores in all 50 states. So there's no sale calendar to wait for before you shop.

Its private brands include Time and Tru and Free Assembly, and almost every store does same-day pickup and delivery. That's handy when you need something for work or school today rather than next week, and it saves the drive.

The trade-off is the brand mix. If you shop Kohl's for national labels next to a store brand, Target is the closer match. It puts Levi's on the same page as its own jeans.
bodies.burlington:
Burlington is the off-price store to try when a coat is on the list. Coats are what it's known for, and it also sells women's, men's and juniors' clothing, a separate plus department, beauty and shoes.

Like Ross, it's in-store only. The website points you to a location rather than a checkout. Its stores cover 47 states, DC and Puerto Rico, close to Kohl's own spread, and the store finder lists them state by state.

If you buy extended sizes, start with that plus department, which gets its own spot on the menu next to Ladies and Juniors. And if you'd rather order your bargains online, TJ Maxx and Marshalls both have websites where Burlington doesn't.
bodies.marshalls:
Marshalls is TJ Maxx's sister store, and the one to choose when shoes or menswear are part of the trip. It sells the same family clothing, beauty and home at off-price, with a full line of footwear for women, men and kids and a bigger men's department.

The same company runs both chains and sets them up to be shopped together. So if one store's racks look thin, the other is worth the drive. Marshalls also sells online.

If designer labels matter more to you than shoes, TJ Maxx's Runway department is the better bet. And if you want a store brand at a fixed price, the way Kohl's does Sonoma, look at Target instead.
bodies.old-navy:
Old Navy is the pick if what you buy at Kohl's is mostly jeans and basics for the family. It's one brand rather than a department store. Its women's jeans run from $34.99 for the Curvy Mid-Rise Wow Bootcut to $69.99 for the Old Navy x Altuzarra High-Waisted Baggy Wide-Leg. Most styles sit between $44.99 and $54.99, across the OG, Vintage Slim and Rockstar lines.

Sizes are the strong point. Jeans go from 00 to 30, with petite and tall, and the Wow line is the cheapest way in. Rewards members get free shipping from $50, and returns run 30 days.

If you want other brands in the same cart, Target puts Levi's next to its own jeans.

closing.heading: How to choose
closing.body: Start with what you go to Kohl's for. If it's the one-stop department store, Macy's and JCPenney are the closest, and a Macy's with a Backstage inside adds the bargain rack. To trade up, Dillard's adds designer denim, and Nordstrom makes buying online painless with free shipping and no return deadline. If the deal is the whole point, TJ Maxx and Marshalls are the off-price pair, with Ross for in-store hunts and Burlington when you need a coat. For everyday basics, Target pairs its own labels with Levi's, Walmart keeps prices low every day, and Old Navy covers jeans from size 00 to 30.

faqs.a: Kohl's sells moderately priced clothing, shoes, accessories, beauty and home goods. Much of it is its own labels, like Sonoma Goods for Life, Croft & Barrow and Apt. 9, sold next to national brands, and its beauty side includes Sephora.

Kohl's Corporation owns it. The company runs more than 1,100 Kohl's stores across 49 states, plus kohls.com, and sells its own brands alongside exclusive lines like LC Lauren Conrad and Simply Vera Vera Wang.
